sentence: The olive tree beaten at harvest keeps *two or three berries* of its tens of thousands (Isaiah 17:6; 24:13); the righteous man is priced above the gold of Ophir while the mass of the house runs to dross (Isaiah 13:12; Ezekiel 22:18); the remnant stands among the nations as the sym:sym-lion[lion] among the beasts of the forest — apex in authority, one or two per thousand in count (Micah 5:8); Job's great household died down to four lone messengers and the man himself (Job 1); Josephus counts six thousand Pharisees in a nation of a million, and Jesus set the bar *above* them (Matthew 5:20); Micaiah stood one against four hundred court prophets (1 Kings 22:6); Moses said it without a figure at all — __“ye were the *fewest of all people*”__ (Deuteronomy 7:7); and 2 Esdras answers our very question: __“The most High hath made this world for many, but the world to come for few.”__ Methods with no way to coordinate with one another — census arithmetic, stated ratios, orchard facts, field geometry, land capacity, ore grades, animal populations, household counts, sect rosters — and every one lands in the same band: *a fraction of one percent, centering near one in five hundred*.

Throughout Scripture, worship is a thing men __“go up”__ to do at appointed times: Elkanah __“went up out of his city *yearly* to worship and to sacrifice unto the LORD of hosts in Shiloh”__ (1 Samuel 1:3); the firstfruits are set down before the altar, __“and worship”__ (Deuteronomy 26:10); Greeks __“came up to *worship at the feast*”__ (John 12:20); the Ethiopian eunuch __“had come to Jerusalem for to worship”__ (Acts 8:27); Paul __“went up to Jerusalem for to worship”__ (Acts 24:11) — and then defines the act for the governor: __“so *worship* I the God of my fathers, sym:sym-belief[believing] all things which are written in the *law* and in the prophets”__ (Acts 24:14).

link:/books/symbolic-language/the-fear-of-the-lord/[Solomon ends his book] on the two clauses this book keeps finding joined — sym:sym-fear[fear] God, and keep his commandments (Ecclesiastes 12:13) — and then: __“For God shall bring every work into *judgment*”__ (Ecclesiastes 12:14).footnote:fn14ecc1213[Solomon's conclusion of the whole matter is derived in the chapter link:/books/symbolic-language/the-fear-of-the-lord/[The Fear of the Lord].] The judgment men fear as an alien terror is nothing but the rulings they were handed at Sinai, applied at last by the Judge who wrote them — __“So speak ye, and so do, as they that shall be judged by the *law of* sym:sym-liberty[liberty]”__ (James 2:12).

ifndef::print-edition[] The two are joined by the sym:sym-cloud[cloud] — water drawn up out of the sea below into the heavens above, and, in the symbol, a multitude link:/books/symbolic-language/clouds/[drawn up out of the peoples].footnote:fn34cloudrise[Derived in the link:/books/symbolic-language/clouds/[Clouds] chapter.] endif::[] ifdef::print-edition[] The two are joined by the sym:sym-cloud[cloud] — water drawn up out of the sea below into the heavens above, and, in the symbol, a multitude drawn up out of the peoples.footnote:fn34cloudrise[Derived in the Clouds study, in the digital edition at https://TimeTested.Bible[TimeTested.Bible].] endif::[] Jeremiah tells us — twice, word for word (Jeremiah 10:13; 51:16) — how the drawing up works:

The corners of the sym:sym-field[field] may not be wholly reaped; they are left standing for the sym:sym-poor[poor] and the sym:sym-stranger[stranger] (Leviticus 19:9-10) — and __“corners”__ is _pe'ah_, link:/books/symbolic-language/wings/[the reserved edge].footnote:fn12peah[The reserved edge — _kanaph_ on the garment, _pe'ah_ in the field — is derived in the link:/books/symbolic-language/wings/[Wings] chapter.] The edge of a field is fixed by mathematics: grain is sown in rows a handbreadth apart, and the perimeter row's share of the crop *shrinks as the field grows* — on the working farms of Israel, five to twenty acres, the reserved edge is a quarter to a half of one percent of the harvest.

The sym:sym-bow[bow] in the cloud is __“the token of the covenant”__ (Genesis 9:12-13 — a chapter of its own ahead); circumcision is __“the sym:sym-sign[sign]… a sym:sym-seal[seal] of the sym:sym-righteousness[righteousness] of the faith”__ (Genesis 17:11; Romans 4:11); the Passover blood on the houses was __“a token”__ (Exodus 12:13); the word of God itself is bound __“for a sign upon thine hand”__ (Deuteronomy 6:8); and the sabbath is __“a sign between me and you throughout your generations… that ye may know that I am the LORD that doth sanctify you… a sign… for ever”__ (Exodus 31:13, 17; Ezekiel 20:12).

Solomon uses the same word for the day the traveling husband returns: __“he will come home at the *full moon*”__ (Proverbs 7:20) — _keseh_ again — and there it is spelled כסא, letter for letter the spelling of _kisse’_, __“throne.”__ The last chapter stood on that identity from the enemy's side; here is the LORD's side of it: both words grow from one root, _kasah_, to cover, to fill — the throne is the covered seat, the full moon the filled light — and Job holds the two senses up in a single verse: __“He holdeth back the face of *his throne*, and spreadeth *his cloud* upon it”__ (Job 26:9), the veiled face of His full sym:sym-moon[moon].

The picture is of __“dawn,”__ __“mist,”__ or __“fog”__ spread over the __“mountains,”__ which is quite common in early morning and aligns with the visual of a __“day of clouds and thick dark mist.”__ The Hebrew word for __“dawn,”__ _shachar_, link:/books/symbolic-language/lucifers-declared-plan/[names the dark before sunrise] — the first light while the sky is still quite dark, before the sun burns away the fog.footnote:fn33shachar[Derived — _shachar_ written on the letters of blackness — in the link:/books/symbolic-language/lucifers-declared-plan/[Lucifer's Declared Plan] chapter.] Now, with the greater context, we have dark clouds of smoke spread over the nations.

The first plague turned the waters of Egypt to blood; the vials turn the sym:sym-sea[sea] and rivers to blood, and this time link:/books/symbolic-language/sea-and-waters/[the interpretation is spoken aloud] (Revelation 16:6).footnote:fn28bloodtodrink[The vial verses are quoted and worked in full in the link:/books/symbolic-language/sea-and-waters/[Sea & Waters] chapter.] The waters are __“peoples, and multitudes, and nations”__ (Revelation 17:15) — the equation the sign-of-Jonah chapter first put to work — so waters turned to blood are death upon the peoples, their own shed blood given back to them; the Sea study in Part Six works the full equation.

The psalm that gave this book the sym:sym-faithful-witness[faithful witness] link:/books/symbolic-language/sun-moon-and-stars/[already sets the throne] as the sym:sym-sun[sun] and as the sym:sym-moon[moon] — Psalm 89:36-37 — plain simile, not wordplay, and the throne is a throne of light.footnote:fn26thronepsalm[Derived in the link:/books/symbolic-language/sun-moon-and-stars/[Sun, Moon, and Stars] chapter.] Where darkness stands near it, it stands *outside*, as a veil: __“clouds and darkness are *round about* him”__ (Psalm 97:2) — round about, not within — the cloud of Job 26:9 spread *upon* the face, holding the light back.

The covering a bride enters when she takes the name is stitched at every corner with the reminder of the law of the One who spreads it — and a bleeding woman once link:/books/symbolic-language/wings/[took hold of that corner] in sym:sym-faith[faith], and the name did what no sound can (Matthew 9:20-21).footnote:fn08wings[The wing, the fringe bound at its corner, and the healing found there are derived in the link:/books/symbolic-language/wings/[Wings] chapter.] The name and the commandments arrive as one garment — which is why the name is kept by keeping the law (Deuteronomy 28:58), and emptied any other way.

Two symbols compound in that phrase: the tree is a nation, and the life is the covenant-existence just defined — so the tree of life is the living nation, the community whose obedience is on display; and what one lays hold of to belong to it is sym:sym-wisdom[wisdom], link:/books/symbolic-language/the-fool-and-the-wise/[the law kept and done] (Deuteronomy 4:6).footnote:fn07deut46[Derived in the chapter link:/books/symbolic-language/the-fool-and-the-wise/[The Fool and the Wise].] (The tree as a symbol of the nation is its own study; here it is enough that the law and the life are bound together.)

He said it to the very leadership whose successors fixed the calendar now defended; He warned His disciples to __“beware of the leaven of the Pharisees”__ — which, Matthew explains, __“is their *doctrine*”__ (Matthew 16:6, 12); Mark records the charge that reaches our question exactly — __“making the word of God of none effect through your *tradition*”__ (Mark 7:13); Paul instructs Titus to give no heed __“to Jewish fables, and commandments of men, that turn from the truth”__ (Titus 1:14), and warns the Colossians against being taken captive __“after the *tradition of men*… and not after Christ”__ (Colossians 2:8).

Beneath the Greek stands a Hebrew word the King James renders both ways, and the wobble is our familiar signpost: __“God did *tempt* Abraham”__ (Genesis 22:1) — the first __“tempt”__ in the Bible, in the very scene that gives us the first __“worship”__ (Genesis 22:5, a discovery the link:/books/symbolic-language/worship/[Worship] chapter will unfold) — is the same word as __“that I may *prove* them”__ over the manna (Exodus 16:4), and __“to *prove* thee… whether thou wouldest *keep his commandments*, or no”__ (Deuteronomy 8:2); David even prays _for_ it: __“*prove* me”__ (Psalm 26:2).

The very night the name is given, God says __“thy name shall not be called any more Jacob”__ (Genesis 35:10) — and then keeps right on calling him Jacob, and names Himself to the end __“the God of Jacob.”__ Isaiah even trades the titles between the two names — __“Israel… my servant, Jacob whom I have chosen”__ (Isaiah 41:8), then __“Jacob my servant; and Israel, whom I have chosen”__ (Isaiah 44:1); and each name runs the whole range, for He __“hath not beheld iniquity in Jacob”__ (Numbers 23:21) and yet __“Israel is defiled”__ (Hosea 5:3).

It is __“cut out… without hands”__ (Daniel 2:45) — and _to cut_ link:/books/symbolic-language/daniel-unsealed/[is the covenant verb] (Genesis 15:18).footnote:fn33karath[Covenants are cut, not made — _karath_ — as the link:/books/symbolic-language/daniel-unsealed/[Daniel Unsealed] chapter showed.] A stone cut by no human hand is a covenant cut by God Himself — and Scripture names the sym:sym-rock[Rock]: __“that sym:sym-rock[Rock] was Christ”__ (1 Corinthians 10:4), the covenant in person; __“the sym:sym-stone[stone] which the builders refused”__ is become __“the head stone of the corner”__ (Psalm 118:22).

God __“doth execute the *judgment* of the fatherless and widow”__ (Deuteronomy 10:18); Israel is told to __“seek judgment, relieve the oppressed, *judge the* sym:sym-fatherless[fatherless], *plead for the* sym:sym-widow[widow]”__ (Isaiah 1:17); and the indictment of the princes is exactly its absence — __“they judge *not* the fatherless, neither doth the cause of the widow come unto them”__ (Isaiah 1:23), __“the *right* of the needy do they not judge”__ (Jeremiah 5:28) — where __“right”__ is _mishpat_ again: the needy man’s judgment is his *due*, the portion God’s law rules to be his.

No lion, no ravenous beast: the beast is a defined symbol — a kingdom of the world, __“the fourth sym:sym-beast[beast] shall be the fourth *kingdom* upon earth”__ (Daniel 7:23) — and the lion is the beast Scripture names a ruler: __“As a roaring sym:sym-lion[lion]… so is a *wicked ruler* over the poor people”__ (Proverbs 28:15); __“her *princes* within her are roaring lions”__ (Zephaniah 3:3); __“Israel is a scattered sym:sym-sheep[sheep]; the *lions* have driven him away: first the *king of Assyria*… and last this *Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon*”__ (Jeremiah 50:17).

If the sea is the peoples, then the people in it are sym:sym-fish[fish] — and Scripture says exactly that: God makes men as the fishes of the sea, creatures with no ruler over them (Habakkuk 1:14) — the scattered, ungoverned mass, exposed to every sym:sym-net[net] link:/books/symbolic-language/the-parables-of-the-kingdom/[dragged through the waters].footnote:fn34fishnet[The fish and the net are derived in the link:/books/symbolic-language/the-parables-of-the-kingdom/[Parables of the Kingdom] chapter.] Now listen to Jesus recruit His disciples, and watch the interpretation arrive in the very next verse:

The derivation stands on the Old Testament the disciples held: the Hebrew _peninim_, which the KJV prints as __“rubies,”__ is by Strong's own definition __“probably a pearl (as round)”__ — sym:sym-wisdom[wisdom] is __“more precious than sym:sym-pearl[pearls]”__ (Proverbs 3:15), her price __“above *pearls*”__ (Job 28:18), and the virtuous woman — the sym:sym-marriage[bride] of a later chapter — is __“far above *pearls*”__ (Proverbs 31:10); the seeker who __“searchest for her as for *hid treasures*”__ (Proverbs 2:4) is the merchant himself, one figure in Solomon's book.

God brings __“many nations”__ against her __“as the sym:sym-sea[sea] causeth his sym:sym-sea[waves] to come up”__ (Ezekiel 26:3) — the nations are the waves; her rulers are __“the princes of the sym:sym-sea[sea]”__ (Ezekiel 26:16); she is __“a merchant of the people for many sym:sym-island[isles]”__ (Ezekiel 27:3) — her cargo is people; and her prince boasts, __“I sit in the seat of God, in the midst of the sym:sym-sea[seas]”__ (Ezekiel 28:2) — a throne amid the peoples, claiming God’s chair.

- __keepeth the watch / walkings__ (31:27) — _tsofiyah_, the watchman's verb (“I have made thee a *watchman*,” Ezekiel 3:17); _halichot_, “a walking, a procession” — the family of Job 31:26's moon “*walking* in brightness.” - __maketh her shine / she it is that shall shine / make her shine in the gates__ (31:28, 30, 31) — _halal_, whose base sense is “to *shine*” before it is “to praise” (the King James’ own “when his candle *shined*,” Job 29:3; “the moon walking in brightness” verse sits in the same field): to praise her is to make her shine, and both senses are true at once.

Leaven link:/books/symbolic-language/the-parables-of-the-kingdom/[is corrupt doctrine] working through the whole lump — purged from every house before Passover, banned from every offering on the altar (Exodus 12:15; Leviticus 2:11; Matthew 16:12; 1 Corinthians 5:6-7).footnote:fn36leaven[Derived in the chapter link:/books/symbolic-language/the-parables-of-the-kingdom/[The Parables of the Kingdom].] So the bread offered to God is _unleavened_ — the feast kept __“with the *unleavened* sym:sym-bread[bread] *of sincerity and* sym:sym-truth[truth]”__ (1 Corinthians 5:8) — a pure and unsoured word.

Jonah link:/books/symbolic-language/sign-of-jonah/[went into the same sea and rose]; the Messiah went into the heart of the earth and could not be held by it (Acts 2:24); and every convert enacts the split in baptism, going under into death and coming up in newness of life (Romans 6:4), his sins staying down like Babylon (Micah 7:19).footnote:fn28notrising[The rising half of the contrast is drawn scene by scene in the link:/books/symbolic-language/sign-of-jonah/[Sign of Jonah] chapter.] The waters take everyone; the covenant decides who comes up.

Even so, when he gave the parables of the kingdom his own disciples did not understand, and Jesus rebuked them for it — a fair rebuke, because the keys were already in the Old Testament, the __“dark sayings of old”__ the psalm said he would utter (Mark 4:13; Psalm 78:2-3; Matthew 13:35) — and link:/books/symbolic-language/the-parables-of-the-kingdom/[a chapter ahead sits that exam].footnote:fn01parables[The link:/books/symbolic-language/the-parables-of-the-kingdom/[Parables of the Kingdom] chapter derives each parable of Matthew 13 from the Old Testament alone.]

Fixed dates and weekday-landings, irreconcilable on the continuous week, agree without effort — and the triple-specified count shows itself for what it is: a *checksum*, written into the law the way redundancy is written into all Scripture, so that the true calendar passes silently and every altered one is convicted by its own arithmetic.footnote:fn31ttt[The full case — the month of four sevens, the renewed-moon days, the witnesses for the fixed sixteenth, and the history of who changed what — is _Time Tested Tradition: The Renewed Biblical Calendar_; this chapter shows only the lock the key must fit.]

The shadow of His sym:sym-wings[wings] is where David hides (Psalm 17:8), makes his refuge until calamities pass (Psalm 57:1), and rejoices (Psalm 63:7) — and those wings are the _kanaph_, the edge link:/books/symbolic-language/wings/[where the fringe is bound] as the reminder of the commandments (Numbers 15:38-39).footnote:fn13kanaph[Derived in the link:/books/symbolic-language/wings/[Wings] chapter.] __“The LORD is thy keeper: the LORD is thy *shade* upon thy right hand”__ (Psalm 121:5) — the LORD does not merely cast a shadow; He _is_ the shade.

The Hebrew says only __“after one in the midst”__; __“tree”__ is supplied by the translators — and with it gone, the literal reading has nothing left to name, so it guesses: a sacred tree, a priest in the midst, a deity called __“One.”__ The symbol supplies nothing — __“in the gardens, after one”__ is among the nations, following one — and it reads with the context, for the next verses are the LORD gathering __“all nations and tongues”__ and sending the escaped __“unto the nations”__ (Isaiah 66:18-19).

The __“*bountiful* eye”__ is, in the letters, a *good eye* — טוֹב־עַיִן — and its goodness is giving: __“he giveth of his *bread* to the sym:sym-poor[poor]”__ (Proverbs 22:9); the __“*evil* eye”__ hoards its bread (Proverbs 23:6); and Jesus keeps the same pair in the lamp-saying itself — __“but if thine sym:sym-eye[eye] be *evil*, thy whole body shall be full of sym:sym-darkness[darkness]”__ (Matthew 6:23); __“Is thine eye *evil*, because I am *good*?”__ (Matthew 20:15).

It is the palm God laid over Moses while the glory passed by (Exodus 33:22); and here it is the curved cup that receives the Bridegroom's light and *holds fast the circuit*, carrying it round the year — then opens toward the sym:sym-poor[poor], the King's own signature: __“He shall deliver the needy when he crieth; the *poor* also”__ (Psalm 72:12), in the very psalm where they fear Him __“with the sun and *before the face of* the moon”__ through all revolutions of time (72:5, as the letters run).

_Shachar_, __“morning,”__ is written with the same consonants as the verb Strong's defines __“to be dim or dark (in color)… be black”__ — the dictionary itself derives the dawn-word __“through the idea of the *duskiness* of early dawn.”__ The hour called _shachar_ is the dark before sunrise — Mary came to the tomb __“early, when it was yet dark”__ (John 20:1) — so the fallen shining one is _ben shachar_ in the second sense: the product of the darkness before dawn, a light whose output is sym:sym-darkness[darkness].

Moses wrote __“fear”__; Jesus rendered it __“worship.”__ The Lord Himself treats the two words as one thing — and the rest of Scripture backs His translation in parallel columns: __“him shall ye sym:sym-fear[fear], and him shall ye *worship*, and to him shall ye do sacrifice”__ (2 Kings 17:36); __“O *worship* the LORD in the beauty of holiness: *fear* before him, all the earth”__ (Psalm 96:9); __“Who shall not *fear* thee, O Lord?… all nations shall come and *worship* before thee”__ (Revelation 15:4).

These are gates, not growth curves — and inside the gates He named the marks: __“If ye *continue in my word*, then are ye my disciples *indeed*”__ (John 8:31); __“By this shall all men know that ye are my disciples, if ye have sym:sym-love[love] one to another”__ (John 13:35) — and love is the keeping of the commandments (1 John 5:3); __“Herein is my Father glorified, that ye bear much sym:sym-fruit[fruit]; so shall ye be my disciples”__ (John 15:8) — and fruit is works.

And the oldest translation of all leans the same way: the Septuagint, made centuries before Messiah, renders the day __“in the *glorious* day of your feast”__ — the Greek is _eusēmos_, *well-marked, conspicuous*, built on _sēma_, a *sign*, the very root the Greek of Genesis 1:14 hangs the lights on, __“for *signs*.”__ Whatever else those translators heard in _keseh_, they heard the day the sky cannot hide — and of the moon's phases exactly one is conspicuous, while the dark conjunction is the one day the sky shows no sign at all.

__“Everlasting punishment”__ (Matthew 25:46) is _kolasis_ — from a root meaning *to prune*, the gardener's word, and Jesus drew its picture Himself: the fruitless branch __“is cast forth… and burned”__ (John 15:6) — cut off and consumed, not kept alive in the coals; and __“everlasting”__ (_aiōnios_) marks the permanence of the *result*, exactly as __“eternal redemption”__ (Hebrews 9:12) is a redeeming that happened once and holds forever, and as Sodom, set forth as an example of __“eternal fire”__ (Jude 7), is not burning this afternoon.

* __“the *children of the kingdom* shall be cast out”__ (Matthew 8:12) * the tares — __“all things that offend, and them which do *lawlessness*”__ — gathered *out of His kingdom* (Matthew 13:41-42) * the bad fish, severed __“from among the *just*”__ (Matthew 13:49-50) * the wedding *guest* without the garment (Matthew 22:13) * the *evil servant*, appointed __“his portion with the *hypocrites*”__ (Matthew 24:51) * the *unprofitable servant* (Matthew 25:30) * the ones who __“have eaten and drunk in thy presence”__ (Luke 13:26-28)

That is why Hosea, God’s sign-and-similitude marriage, must not only endure his wife’s adultery but _buy her back_ — __“So I *bought her* to me for fifteen pieces of silver”__ (Hosea 3:2) — and why the reunion is a fresh betrothal in the vocabulary this book keeps finding at the center: __“I will *betroth thee* unto me for ever; yea, I will betroth thee unto me in sym:sym-righteousness[righteousness], and in sym:sym-judgment[judgment]… and thou shalt sym:sym-knowing[know] the LORD”__ (Hosea 2:19-20).

The passage is Isaiah 61:1-2, and its closing proclamation — __“the *acceptable* sym:sym-year[year] *of the LORD*”__ — is the *year of release*, link:/books/symbolic-language/liberty/[the seventh year of Deuteronomy 15], when debts are cancelled and captives go free.footnote:fn05release[The full derivation is in the link:/books/symbolic-language/liberty/[Liberty] chapter.] The gospel, in Jesus’ own chosen words, is a royal proclamation of release — and He sat down and told them, __“This day is this scripture fulfilled in your ears”__ (Luke 4:21).

That is why __“the sand of the sea”__ is Scripture’s byword for a multitude past numbering: Abraham’s seed __“as the sym:sym-sand[sand] which is upon the sym:sym-sea[sea] shore”__ (Genesis 22:17); Israel __“as the sym:sym-sand[sand] of the sym:sym-sea[sea], which cannot be measured nor numbered”__ (Hosea 1:10); and the last enemy horde, Gog and Magog, __“the number of whom is as the sym:sym-sand[sand] of the sym:sym-sea[sea]”__ (Revelation 20:8).

The sym:sym-mountain[mountain] is an empire, and Scripture knows one mountain that link:/books/symbolic-language/mountain/[holds all the kingdoms at once]: the destroying mountain that destroys all the earth (Jeremiah 51:25) — sym:sym-babel[Babylon], the composite kingdom.footnote:fn31mountain[The mountain-as-kingdom derivation — Jeremiah 51:25 beside Daniel 2 and Revelation 17 — is made in the link:/books/symbolic-language/mountain/[Mountain] chapter.] And the offer arrives priced in Babylon's own doom-unit: he shows the kingdoms in a *moment* — the very measure by which they fall.

The rains run on the covenant's calendar: __“I will give you the rain of your land *in his due season*, the *first rain* and the *latter rain*”__ — for obedience (Deuteronomy 11:14); __“he shall come unto us *as the rain*, as the *latter and former rain* unto the earth”__ (Hosea 6:3) — the LORD Himself arriving on the rain's own schedule; __“he hath given you the *former rain* moderately, and he will cause to come down for you… the former rain, and the *latter rain*”__ (Joel 2:23).

The two dominions have their peoples: the children of sym:sym-light[light] and of the sym:sym-day[day] — the households link:/books/symbolic-language/light-and-darkness/[the Light and Darkness chapter divided] (1 Thessalonians 5:5).footnote:fn24households[Derived in the link:/books/symbolic-language/light-and-darkness/[Light and Darkness] chapter.] The day's children are the covenant righteous; the night is where the nations sit — __“Galilee of the *Gentiles*; the people which sat in sym:sym-darkness[darkness] saw great sym:sym-light[light]”__ (Matthew 4:15-16).

That spread skirt is the _kanaph_, the sym:sym-wings[wing], link:/books/symbolic-language/wings/[doing both of its offices]: the edge that carries the fringe bound as the reminder to keep the commandments and do them (Numbers 15:39), and the shade a refuge shelters under.footnote:fn37kanaph[The kanaph — wing, skirt, border, corner — and the fringe at its edge are derived in the link:/books/symbolic-language/wings/[Wings] chapter.] The covenant contains the commands; faithfulness to them gains the covering — and what it covers is the nakedness, the sin.

Liberty as license — __“liberty for an occasion to the flesh”__ (Galatians 5:13), __“liberty for a cloke of maliciousness”__ (1 Peter 2:16) — is not liberty misused; it is the old master’s brand under a new name, for __“whosoever committeth sym:sym-sin[sin] is the servant of sin.”__ The offer of freedom from God’s rule is the serpent’s original sales pitch, and it has never once delivered: the man who escapes the law of liberty does not walk free, he walks back into the slaver’s house.

The money is called __“a *memorial*”__ (Exodus 30:16) — the same word the law uses for the sign bound between the eyes (on the forehead) — and it is not banked but appointed __“for the service of the tabernacle.”__ Appointed how, Exodus records to the shekel: __“of the hundred talents of silver were *cast the sockets of the sanctuary*, and the sockets of the vail; … a talent for a socket”__ (Exodus 38:25-27) — a half-shekel a head for 603,550 counted men, melted into the foundations.

The made thing men serve takes a fixed political shape in the Bible’s symbolic language: the sym:sym-beast[beast], a kingdom of men — a different Greek word, but the same structure, for a kingdom is as much a made thing as a carved one — so that creature-worship comes to its head exactly where this chapter is going: __“all the world… worshipped the beast”__ (Revelation 13:3-4), and the everlasting gospel answers by naming God by the one act no creature shares: __“worship him that *made*.”__

The thrones are *set* — placed like lights in their stations.footnote:dan79set[The King James prints __“the thrones were cast down”__; the Aramaic verb is one of placing, and the newer translations read it so — the thrones were set, not overthrown.] And the title under __“Ancient of days”__ is built on a root of moving onward, going before — read once, He is the Ancient of Days; read again, He is the *Foremost of Days*: the One at the head of the days, seated where the days begin.

The kingdom is a sym:sym-mountain[mountain] and the peoples a sym:sym-sea[sea]; the sym:sym-gospel[gospel] is the renewed covenant, the law going forth from Zion; the sym:sym-way[way], the sym:sym-truth[truth], and the sym:sym-life[life] are that law walked; the sym:sym-name[name] is the covenant owned, the sym:sym-garment[garment] the righteousness worn, the sym:sym-light[light] the covenant made visible; the wise are those who do it, and the fools those who do not.

Ask it what _porneia_ means and the answer is just as confident: __“the broad New Testament term for illicit sexual activity or ‘sexual immorality’ — any form of sexual intercourse or behavior outside the covenant of monogamous marriage.”__ Press further and the scholarship divides into three camps — most read the exception as any serious sexual sin; some confine it to sin discovered during betrothal, like Joseph’s dilemma; a few tie it to the forbidden unions of Leviticus 18 — and the survey closes the way surveys do: the majority view prevails.

The man __“had not on a wedding garment”__ (Matthew 22:11), and when the king asks how he entered so, he has no answer; __“he was speechless”__ (Matthew 22:12) — the Greek is stronger than the English: _phimoō_, to *muzzle*, the same word Paul uses of the ox that treads out the grain (1 Corinthians 9:9) and the very word Jesus speaks to the storm and to unclean spirits, __“Peace, be still”__ (Mark 4:39), __“Hold thy peace”__ (Mark 1:25).

In the end the sea even yields up its wealth to Zion: __“the abundance of the sym:sym-sea[sea] shall be converted unto thee, the forces of the Gentiles shall come unto thee”__ (Isaiah 60:5) — the verse glossing itself once more, the abundance of the sea being the Gentiles — and Moses had promised exactly that, when the tribes would __“call the people unto the sym:sym-mountain[mountain]”__ and __“suck of the abundance of the sym:sym-sea[seas]”__ (Deuteronomy 33:19).

The Son thus relives the nation’s story, and where Israel fell, He stands: through the water — as all Israel was __“baptized… in the sym:sym-cloud[cloud] and in the sym:sym-sea[sea]”__ (1 Corinthians 10:2, a crossing the sym:sym-sea[Sea & Waters] chapter will read) — then forty days fasting in the wilderness answering Israel’s forty years (Matthew 4:2), turning the tempter away each time with words drawn from the very chapters Moses wrote about those years (Deuteronomy 8:3; 6:16; 6:13).

The link:/books/symbolic-language/the-parables-of-the-kingdom/[Parables of the Kingdom] chapter already dug them out from under the King James’ __“rubies”__: the Hebrew _peninim_ is, by Strong's own definition, __“probably *a pearl* (as round).”__ Recovered, the pearls keep exactly the parable's company: sym:sym-wisdom[Wisdom] is priced above *pearls* (Proverbs 3:15; 8:11; Job 28:18) — and the seeker who searches for her __“as for *hid treasures*”__ (Proverbs 2:4) is himself the merchant of the parable.

The book of 2 Esdras, wrestling with exactly our question, stacks analogy on analogy: __“The most High hath made this world for many, but the world to come for few”__; the lost outnumber the saved __“like as a wave is greater than a drop”__; and God keeps __“a grape of the cluster… and a plant of a great people,”__ one grape from a cluster of hundreds, kept and perfected __“with great labour”__ (2 Esdras 8:1; 9:15-16, 21-22).

In stone: Solomon raises the temple __“for my name.”__ And in covenant: the Son of David builds the house the first two only sketched — __“Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it up… he spake of the *temple of his body*”__ (John 2:19-21); __“ye also, as lively sym:sym-stone[stones], are *built up a spiritual house*”__ (1 Peter 2:5); __“Christ as a son over his own house; *whose house are we*”__ (Hebrews 3:6).

And judgment is a thing _given to_ the saints as an inheritance: __“*judgment was given* to the saints of the most High; and the time came that the saints *possessed the kingdom*”__ (Daniel 7:22) — thrones, in Revelation’s replay of that scene: __“I saw thrones, and they sat upon them, and *judgment was given* unto them… and they lived and *reigned* with Christ”__ (Revelation 20:4); __“ye also shall sit upon twelve thrones, *judging* the twelve tribes of Israel”__ (Matthew 19:28).

The life _was_ the light — and light is a defined symbol with link:/books/symbolic-language/light-and-darkness/[its own chapter ahead]: not truth in the abstract, but the law lived where men can see it (Matthew 5:16).footnote:fn07light516[Derived in the link:/books/symbolic-language/light-and-darkness/[Light and Darkness] chapter.] So John’s equation compounds the symbols: the covenant-existence, held perfectly in Him, was itself the lived example — obedience demonstrated in the open, where men could watch it and walk by it.

The manna was a similitude of __“the true sym:sym-bread[bread] from heaven”__ (John 6:32) — and the feeding of the five thousand that opens that discourse is itself a lived sign: John calls it one (the __“miracle”__ of John 6:14 is the Greek _sēmeion_), the sign the last chapter read in full — the Law carried by witnesses, feeding the famished — and the sym:sym-sea[Sea & Waters] chapter ahead will deepen the sym:sym-fish[fish]’s half of its key.

sym:sym-leaven[Leaven] is purged from every house before the feast (Exodus 12:15); it is banned from the altar absolutely — __“ye shall burn *no leaven*… in any offering of the LORD made by fire”__ (Leviticus 2:11); Amos names a leavened offering in sarcasm to a rebellious people — __“offer a sacrifice of thanksgiving *with leaven*… for this *liketh you*”__ (Amos 4:5); and Hosea watches adulterous Ephraim rise like dough, the baker idle __“until it be leavened”__ (Hosea 7:4).

__“She is a tree of life to them that lay hold upon her: and blessed is every one that holdeth her fast”__ (3:18) — the holding-verb is _tamak_, the verb of the palms holding the circuit, and the verb of Moses’ hands on the mountain, held up *steady* — _emunah_, the faithful-witness word — __“until the going down of the sun,”__ while Joshua *weakened* Amalek — _chalash_, the rare verb of Isaiah 14:12, three occurrences in all of Scripture (Exodus 17:12-13).

Micah has just invoked the Exodus — __“according to the days of thy coming out of the land of Egypt”__ (Micah 7:15) — so the picture is exact: our sins go down like Pharaoh’s army, cast into the sea, link:/books/symbolic-language/the-fall-of-babylon/[never to rise].footnote:fn34neverrise[Why the verdict is the not-rising — Babylon sinks and shall not rise; the righteous come up — is proved in the link:/books/symbolic-language/the-fall-of-babylon/[Fall of Babylon] chapter.]

The link:/books/symbolic-language/sun-moon-and-stars/[Sun, Moon, and Stars] chapter read the lights: the sym:sym-sun[sun] the Father and the husband; the sym:sym-moon[moon] the sym:sym-faithful-witness[faithful witness] — the Son toward His Father, the sym:sym-marriage[bride] toward her Bridegroom; the sym:sym-stars[stars] the righteous, gathered into the twelve; the sym:sym-elders[elders] seated among the host; and the gates of the sky's tabernacle, through which the lights come and go.

The field is the world by the Teacher's own key, and the buyer purchases *all of it* to possess the treasure — a price One alone paid: __“though he was sym:sym-rich[rich]… he became sym:sym-poor[poor]”__ (2 Corinthians 8:9), __“the propitiation… for the sym:sym-sin[sins] of the whole world”__ (1 John 2:2) — and the treasure was defined at Sinai before the parable ever borrowed it: the *people* are the treasure, and the seeker is God.

When the threshed wheat is thrown up into the wind, the light, empty *chaff* is carried off while the heavy grain falls back to the floor — and this is what the wicked are likened to, weightless and rootless: the chaff which the sym:sym-wind[wind] drives away (Psalm 1:4), __“chased as the chaff of the sym:sym-mountain[mountains] before the wind”__ (Isaiah 17:13) — the very kingdoms of the link:/books/symbolic-language/mountain/[Mountain] chapter, blown off like husks.

The word under Daniel's __“weeks”__ is the name of a feast — _Shavuot_, the Feast of sym:sym-week[Weeks], the Feast of Sevens — and that feast is counted exactly the way the jubilee is counted: __“seven sabbaths shall be complete: even unto the morrow after the seventh sabbath shall ye number *fifty days*”__ (Leviticus 23:15-16), as the jubilee numbers __“seven sabbaths of sym:sym-year[years]”__ and hallows __“the *fiftieth year*”__ (Leviticus 25:8, 10).

link:/books/symbolic-language/the-parables-of-the-kingdom/[The rain is doctrine] — Moses’ teaching dropping as the rain, Isaiah's word coming down from heaven to give sym:sym-seed[seed] to the sower and sym:sym-bread[bread] to the eater (Deuteronomy 32:2; Isaiah 55:10-11).footnote:fn30rain[Derived in the chapter link:/books/symbolic-language/the-parables-of-the-kingdom/[The Parables of the Kingdom].] The cloud is the vehicle; the rain is the word it was sent to pour.

Jesus reads history the same way, time after time: __“as the days of Noe were, so shall also the coming of the Son of man be”__ (Matthew 24:37); __“as it was in the days of Lot… even thus shall it be in the day when the Son of man is revealed”__ (Luke 17:28, 30); __“as Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness, even so must the Son of man be lifted up”__ (John 3:14).

The Jew is __“one inwardly”__ (Romans 2:28-29) — and Paul's definition carries Judah's name inside it: Judah means *praise* — __“Now will I *praise* the LORD: therefore she called his name Judah”__ (Genesis 29:35) — and the verse lands exactly there: the Jew inwardly is he __“whose *praise* is not of men, but of God.”__ The word wears three coats — ethnic, religious, covenant — and as with every symbol, the context tells you which one it is wearing.

Ezekiel's __“dwell”__ is _shakan_, the tabernacle word, and Matthew's Greek keeps it — _kataskēnoō_, to pitch one's tent — and the prophets had promised the nations exactly that tent-rest in a Person: __“a *Branch* shall grow out of his roots… and in that day there shall be a root of Jesse… to it shall the *Gentiles* seek: and his *rest* shall be glorious”__ (Isaiah 11:1, 10); __“Behold the man whose name is The *BRANCH*”__ (Zechariah 6:12).

Job wore it: __“I put on sym:sym-righteousness[righteousness], and it clothed me: my *judgment* was as a robe and a diadem”__ — and then the inventory of what the sym:sym-garment[garment] was made of: __“I delivered the poor that cried, and the fatherless… I was eyes to the blind, and feet was I to the lame… a father to the poor: and the cause which I knew not I *searched out*”__ (Job 29:12-16).

The law forbids wholly reaping the sym:sym-wings[corners] of the sym:sym-field[field]; they are left for the sym:sym-poor[poor] and the sym:sym-stranger[stranger] (Leviticus 19:9-10) — and __“corners”__ is _pe'ah_, link:/books/symbolic-language/wings/[the reserved edge].footnote:fn12peahweb[The reserved edge — _kanaph_ on the garment, _pe'ah_ in the field — is derived in the link:/books/symbolic-language/wings/[Wings] chapter.] The edge of a field is fixed by mathematics.

The waters below are the peoples; the vapour God draws up out of the sea is people drawn up out of the mass; and the multitude gathered in the heavens is exactly what John sees before the throne — __“a sym:sym-sea[sea of glass] like unto crystal”__ (Revelation 4:6), with __“them that had gotten the victory over the sym:sym-beast[beast]”__ standing on it, __“having the harps of God”__ (Revelation 15:2).

The truth link:/books/symbolic-language/the-way-the-truth-and-the-life/[is God’s law itself] — __“thy law is the sym:sym-truth[truth]”__ (Psalm 119:142).footnote:fn32truthlaw[Derived in the chapter link:/books/symbolic-language/the-way-the-truth-and-the-life/[The Way, The Truth, and The Life].] With this definition, Hebrews 10:26 can be understood to say __“if we sin willfully after we have received knowledge of the law (of Moses)”__.

The text supplies its own label for the fate of the lost, and the label is not __“the second torment.”__ It is __“the second *death*”__ — and the Hebrew Revelation of the Cochin manuscripts sharpens the word: in three of its four occurrences the phrase is _acher maveth_, *another* death, a death of a *different kind* — the word used for taking __“another”__ wife (Exodus 21:10) and for Caleb's __“another spirit”__ (Numbers 14:24).

Ruth arrives in Bethlehem carrying every name of the gleaning household at once: poor — __“I went out full, and the LORD hath brought me home again empty”__ (Ruth 1:21); a sym:sym-stranger[stranger] — __“seeing I am a stranger”__ (Ruth 2:10); a sym:sym-widow[widow], her husband dead (Ruth 1:5); fatherless in every practical sense, having __“left thy father and thy mother, and the land of thy nativity”__ (Ruth 2:11).

Some forty writers, across some fifteen centuries, in multiple languages, hold one symbol grammar without a collision — as the chapters ahead will prove: the sym:sym-mountain[mountain] is a kingdom from Moses to Daniel's Babylon to John's Patmos; the sym:sym-seed[seed] is the word in Isaiah's field and in the boat on Galilee; the sym:sym-harlot[harlot], the sym:sym-olive[vine], the shepherds, the sym:sym-wings[wings] keep their meanings across authors who never met.

The high priest's mitre carried a graven plate __“upon Aaron's *forehead*,”__ reading HOLINESS TO THE LORD, __“that they may be *accepted*”__ (Exodus 28:36-38); the word is bound __“as frontlets *between thine eyes*”__ (Deuteronomy 6:8); and the redeemed wear __“his sym:sym-name[name]… in their foreheads”__ (Revelation 22:4) — while the counterfeit is issued for the same head: the beast's mark __“in their foreheads”__ (Revelation 13:16).

The world's kingdoms are not transferred; they fall — Daniel's sym:sym-stone[stone] grinds them to sym:sym-chaff[chaff] and the sym:sym-wind[wind] carries them off, no place found for them (Daniel 2:35) — and what is given to the Son is another kingdom entirely, the kingdom the God of heaven sets up to break and consume all these (Daniel 2:44): __“there was *given him* dominion, and glory, and a kingdom”__ (Daniel 7:14).

- __taketh it__ (31:16) — the written verb is _laqach_, to *take*; the King James prints __“buyeth it.”__ - __the covenant's meat / the appointed portion__ (31:15) — _teref_ is the noun of Psalm 111:5, “he hath given *meat* unto them that fear him: he will ever be mindful of his *covenant*”; _choq_ is “an enactment; an appointment (of time)” — the King James’ own “set time” (Job 14:13), and the word of Jeremiah 31:35's moon-and-stars ordinances.

The destroying verb of the verse is singular, and link:/books/symbolic-language/daniel-unsealed/[its subject is the Messiah]: he will destroy the people of the coming ruler, __“and the end thereof shall be with a sym:sym-flood[flood]”__ (Daniel 9:26).footnote:fn34dan926[The word-by-word case for this reading — the singular verb, its subject, and the seventy sevens entire — is made in the link:/books/symbolic-language/daniel-unsealed/[Daniel Unsealed] chapter.]
